'''Eli M. Pearce''' (May 1, 1929 – May 18, 2015) was research professor at [[New York University Polytechnic School of Engineering]] and a past-president of the [[American Chemical Society]]. He received a B.S. degree in chemistry from [[Brooklyn College]] in 1949. Pearce earned a Ph.D. in chemistry from [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]] (now NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering). He published more than 250 papers on his research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://engineering.nyu.edu/news/2014/08/19/american-chemical-society-gives-professor-eli-pearce-rock-star-chemistry-honor|title=American Chemical Society Gives Professor Eli Pearce Rock Star of Chemistry Honor|work=NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering|date=19 August 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Eli_Pearce2|title=Eli M Pearce|work=ResearchGate}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Professor Eli M. Pearce Sixty Years Dedicated to Sceince|last=Zaikov|first=Gennady|volume=3|issue=1|year=2009|journal=Chemistry and Chemical Technology|url=http://old.lp.edu.ua/fileadmin/ICCT/journal/Vol.3/Num.1/12.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150704201656/http://old.lp.edu.ua/fileadmin/ICCT/journal/Vol.3/Num.1/12.pdf|archive-date=2015-07-04|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/93/web/2015/05/Eli-Pearce-Dies-86.html|title=Eli Pearce Dies At 86|author=Susan J. Ainsworth|work=acs.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/nytimes/obituary.aspx?n=eli-pearce&pid=174905133&fhid=2058|title=ELI PEARCE|work=New York Times}}</ref> He designed fire-resistant polymers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://archive.poly.edu/poly_ebriefs/archives/Feb03.htm#DID |title=EPoly Briefs Home |access-date=2016-10-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304225948/http://archive.poly.edu/poly_ebriefs/archives/Feb03.htm#DID |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
